The First Rule of Preserving Code Leaks

The first rule you should follow is not to talk about or share links to something you've found until you've downloaded it and mirrored it somewhere! If it blows up and makes it into the news, or if the news lies about what's there (like with BetaArchive), it may get taken down before you even get to look at it.

Mirroring

For fast mirroring, sites like anonfile and mega are good, but generally sharing via torrent and seeding with a seedbox or VPN is the best idea.

For super sensitive things, consider using password protected, encrypted 7zip files so that filters and censors can't find them. For git repos, mirror at repo.or.cz and bitbucket, both tend to get fewer DMCA and other legal threats.

Fresh Leaks

If you read a news article, tweet, or blog post about a new leak, scramble to find and copy it! Whenever something is reported on, it will go down fast!

Places To Look

  • BTDig
  • BTDB
  • For Games, RageZone (the mods are assholes)
  • https://archive.fo/
  • https://web.archive.org - (use wildcard searches - http://somesite.com/*)
  • Github (even using the built in search)
  • Bitbucket

  • ftp indexing sites
  • Open directories
